claim: IL-37 is not expressed in mice.
source: The anti-inflammatory cytokine interleukin-37 (IL-37) belongs to the IL-1 family but is not expressed in mice.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as established knowledge about IL-37 expression in mice.

source: We used a human IL-37 (hIL-37tg) expressing mouse, which has been subjected to various models of local and systemic inflammation as well as immunological challenges.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and references previous studies with this mouse model.

claim: Previous studies reveal an immunomodulatory role of IL-37, which can be characterized as an important suppressor of innate immunity.
source: Previous studies reveal an immunomodulatory role of IL-37, which can be characterized as an important suppressor of innate immunity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a summary of previous research findings.

evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: In wild-type mice, activated microglial phenotype was observed after LPS injection.
source: In wild-type mice, decreased spine density, activated microglial phenotype and impaired long-term potentiation (LTP) were observed after LPS injection, whereas hIL-37tg mice showed no impairment.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: In wild-type mice, impaired long-term potentiation (LTP) was observed after LPS injection.
source: In wild-type mice, decreased spine density, activated microglial phenotype and impaired long-term potentiation (LTP) were observed after LPS injection, whereas hIL-37tg mice showed no impairment.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: hIL-37tg mice showed no impairment in spine density, microglial phenotype, or LTP after LPS injection.
source: In wild-type mice, decreased spine density, activated microglial phenotype and impaired long-term potentiation (LTP) were observed after LPS injection, whereas hIL-37tg mice showed no impairment.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: Expression of IL-37 is able to limit inflammation in the brain after acute inflammatory events.
source: Our results show that expression of IL-37 is able to limit inflammation in the brain after acute inflammatory events and prevent loss of cognitive abilities in a mouse model of AD.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the study's results.

claim: Expression of IL-37 prevents loss of cognitive abilities in a mouse model of AD.
source: Our results show that expression of IL-37 is able to limit inflammation in the brain after acute inflammatory events and prevent loss of cognitive abilities in a mouse model of AD.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the study's results.

claim: Neuroinflammation is characterized by glial cell activation and is mediated via pro-inflammatory signals.
source: Neuroinflammation is characterized by glial cell activation and is mediated via pro-inflammatory signals (Ji et al., 2014; Rivest, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Acute inflammation is the initial response of the immune system and is characterized by activation of immune cells, rapid production of various cytokines and chemokines, and phagocytic mechanisms.
source: In general, acute inflammation is the initial response of the immune system and is characterized by activation of immune cells, rapid production of various cytokines and chemokines, and phagocytic mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about acute inflammation.

claim: Persistent inflammation can lead to a pathophysiological state that results in tissue damage and loss of function.
source: Although these processes are important to combat pathogens, persistent inflammation can lead to a pathophysiological state that results in tissue damage and loss of function.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about persistent inflammation.

claim: Pro-inflammatory cytokines include interleukin (IL)–1β and tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α).
source: Examples of pro-inflammatory cytokines include interleukin (IL)–1β and tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α), both of which elicit a strong acute inflammatory response (Dinarello, 1996; Leal et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: IL-1β and TNF-α elicit a strong acute inflammatory response.
source: Examples of pro-inflammatory cytokines include interleukin (IL)–1β and tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α), both of which elicit a strong acute inflammatory response (Dinarello, 1996; Leal et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Anti-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-4, IL-10, or IL-37 inhibit the action of pro-inflammatory cytokines and hence limit inflammation.
source: In contrast, anti-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-4, IL-10 (De Beaux et al., 1996; Marie et al., 1996), or IL-37 (Nold et al., 2010) inhibit the action of pro-inflammatory cytokines and hence limit inflammation (Cavaillon, 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Long-term activation of glial cells leads to neuroinflammation, which is an important hallmark of many neurological disorders, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease or multiple sclerosis.
source: In the CNS, long-term activation of glial cells leads to neuroinflammation, which is an important hallmark of many neurological disorders, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease or multiple sclerosis (Ji et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: AD is the most common form of dementia characterized by amyloid-β plaques and neurofibrillary tangles in the brain tissue.
source: In particular, AD is the most common form of dementia characterized by amyloid-β plaques and neurofibrillary tangles in the brain tissue.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about AD.

claim: Patients with AD suffer from memory loss, speech disorders, confusion, problems with attention, and spatial orientation.
source: Patients with AD suffer from memory loss, speech disorders, confusion, problems with attention, and spatial orientation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about AD symptoms.

claim: There are currently no effective treatment strategies to combat AD.
source: Currently, there are no effective treatment strategies to combat AD despite the considerable clinical need.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as current knowledge about AD treatment.

claim: Innate immune responses and neuroinflammation are thought to contribute significantly to the progression of AD.
source: Innate immune responses and neuroinflammation are thought to contribute significantly to the progression of AD (Tan et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: The release of IL-1β under pathological conditions can lead to deficits in learning and memory processes as well as in long-term potentiation (LTP).
source: For example, the release of IL-1β under pathological conditions can lead to deficits in learning and memory processes as well as in long-term potentiation (LTP) (Avital et al., 2003; Hein et al., 2010; Tong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) have been associated with impairments in hippocampal neuron structure and function during viral infection.
source: In addition, pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) have been associated with impairments in hippocampal neuron structure and function during viral infection (Hosseini et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: In chronic inflammation, the homeostasis of pro- and anti-inflammatory mediators is completely disturbed.
source: It is important to note that in chronic inflammation, the homeostasis of pro- and anti-inflammatory mediators is completely disturbed and must be therapeutically directed at attenuating persistent inflammatory processes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about chronic inflammation.

claim: Both IL-1α and IL-1β play a role in autoinflammatory, autoimmune, infectious, and degenerative diseases.
source: Among the important pro-inflammatory mediators, both IL-1α and IL-1β play a role in autoinflammatory, autoimmune, infectious, and degenerative diseases (Dinarello, 2009; Dinarello, 2010; Dinarello et al., 2012; Gabay et al., 2010; Sims and Smith, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: IL-1α and IL-1β are structurally related proteins that bind to the type I interleukin 1 receptor (IL-1R1) and elicit similar innate responses.
source: Although IL-1α and IL-1β are encoded by different genes, both cytokines are structurally related proteins that bind to the type I interleukin 1 receptor (IL-1R1) and elicit similar innate responses.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about IL-1α and IL-1β.

claim: IL-1α is constitutively present in healthy cells but is only released under cell stress conditions.
source: However, IL-1α is constitutively present in healthy cells but is only released under cell stress conditions, as is the case during inflammation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about IL-1α.

claim: IL-1β is not present in the healthy state and requires processing by caspase-1 to become active.
source: In contrast, IL-1β is not present in the healthy state; the IL-1β precursor is not active but requires processing by caspase-1, an intracellular protease, resulting in conversion to an active cytokine that is secreted (Garlanda et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: IL-37 and IL-38 act as anti-inflammatory signalling agents and are thought to dampen an ongoing innate immune response.
source: Unlike most members of the IL-1 family that induce inflammation, this important cytokine family also includes two members (IL-37 and IL-38) that act as anti-inflammatory signalling agents and are thought to dampen an ongoing innate immune response (Nold et al., 2010; Dinarello, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: IL-37 serves as a potent mediator to limit the inflammatory responses.
source: In particularly, IL-37 serves as a potent mediator to limit the inflammatory responses (Cavalli and Dinarello, 2018; Caraffa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: A transgenic mouse model expressing the human splice variant IL-37b (hIL-37tg) was developed.
source: Therefore, a transgenic mouse model expressing the human splice variant IL-37b (hIL-37tg) was developed (Nold et al., 2010; Cavalli and Dinarello, 2018) and showed potent anti-inflammatory and beneficial effects in a wide variety of different pathological conditions in different organs (Nold et al., 2010; Ballak et al., 2014; Coll-Miró et al., 2016; McNamee et al., 2011; Yousif et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The hIL-37tg mouse showed potent anti-inflammatory and beneficial effects in a wide variety of different pathological conditions in different organs.
source: Therefore, a transgenic mouse model expressing the human splice variant IL-37b (hIL-37tg) was developed (Nold et al., 2010; Cavalli and Dinarello, 2018) and showed potent anti-inflammatory and beneficial effects in a wide variety of different pathological conditions in different organs (Nold et al., 2010; Ballak et al., 2014; Coll-Miró et al., 2016; McNamee et al., 2011; Yousif et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The transgenic mouse was generated to allow continuous expression of IL-37 in almost all cells using the full-length cDNA of IL-37b through the CMV promoter.
source: The transgenic mouse was generated to allow continuous expression of IL-37 in almost all cells. This was achieved by using the full-length cDNA of IL-37b through the CMV promoter (Nold et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: IL-37tg mice did not exhibit an abnormal phenotype and reproduced normally.
source: It is important to note that these IL-37tg mice did not exhibit an abnormal phenotype and reproduced normally (Nold et al., 2010; Dinarello et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: IL-37 binds to the IL-18 receptor (IL-18R) and does not elicit a pro-inflammatory immune response but prevents it and is involved in an anti-inflammatory response.
source: IL-37 has been described as a protein that binds to the IL-18 receptor (IL-18R) and, unlike IL-18, does not elicit a pro-inflammatory immune response but prevents it and is even involved in an anti-inflammatory response (Cavalli and Dinarello, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: IL-37 binds the alpha chain of the IL-18R and additionally interacts with IL-1R8 (also known as TIR8 or SIGIRR) rather than recruiting the beta chain of the IL-18R.
source: IL-37 binds the alpha chain of the IL-18R and additionally interacts with IL-1R8 (also known as TIR8 or SIGIRR) rather than recruiting the beta chain of the IL-18R (as is the case with IL-18 binding) (Nold-Petry et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: The co-localization of IL-37 with IL-18Rα and IL-1R8 was demonstrated in mouse cells.
source: This co-localization was also demonstrated in mouse cells (Nold-Petry et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: The mRNA of IL-18Rα and SIGIRR receptors is present on astrocytes and microglia.
source: Other studies showed the mRNA of IL-18Rα and SIGIRR receptors on astrocytes and microglia (Andre et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: IL-18Rα is expressed on astrocytes and microglia, and IL-18 is produced only by microglial cells.
source: Notably, IL-18Rα has been shown to be expressed on astrocytes and microglia, and IL-18 is produced only by microglial cells, suggesting a signalling cascade running mainly through microglia with respect to IL-18 and IL-37 (Andre et al., 2005; Tsilioni et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Two recent studies focusing on the central and peripheral nervous systems have demonstrated the therapeutic potential of IL-37 in autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and multiple sclerosis (MS).
source: In addition, two recent studies focusing on the central and peripheral nervous systems have demonstrated the therapeutic potential of IL-37 in autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and multiple sclerosis (MS) (Tsilioni et al., 2019; Cavalli et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Tsilioni et al., 2019 demonstrated a reducing effect of inflammation on IL-37 expression in cultured human microglia.
source: Tsilioni et al., 2019 have demonstrated a reducing effect of inflammation on IL-37 expression in cultured human microglia.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: Despite strong activation of the CMV promoter, expression of IL-37 could not be detected in a mouse cell line due to rapid mRNA degradation.
source: Bufler et al., 2004 showed that despite strong activation of the CMV promoter, expression of IL-37 could not be detected (Bufler et al., 2004). It was also shown that the specific mRNA was rapidly degraded.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: A significant and rapid increase in IL-37 mRNA could be achieved by an LPS stimulus.
source: However, a significant and rapid increase in IL-37 mRNA could be achieved by an LPS stimulus (Bufler et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: Administration of recombinant IL-37 frequently exhibited beneficial effects on the outcome of various animal models of human diseases.
source: Similarly, administration of recombinant IL-37 frequently exhibited beneficial effects on the outcome of various animal models of human diseases (Cavalli et al., 2016; Coll-Miró et al., 2016; Moretti et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: IL-37 has been shown to regulate cellular metabolism after an inflammatory stimulus.
source: In addition, IL-37 has been shown to regulate cellular metabolism after an inflammatory stimulus (Su and Tao, 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citation.

claim: Metabolic changes have been described as an important determinant of immunological processes, as shown in macrophages after LPS stimulation.
source: In the last decade, metabolic changes have been described as an important determinant of immunological processes, as shown in macrophages after LPS stimulation (Su and Tao, 2021; O'Neill and Hardie, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The LPS-induced increase in mTOR phosphorylation and decreased AMP-activated protein kinase activity were reversed by expression of IL-37.
source: The LPS-induced increase in mTOR phosphorylation and decreased AMP-activated protein kinase activity were reversed by expression of IL-37 (Nold et al., 2010; Ballak et al., 2014; Nold-Petry et al., 2015; Su and Tao, 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Microglial cells from homozygous IL-37 transgenic (IL-37tg/tg) mice secreted significantly reduced amounts of IL-6 compared to microglial cells from control mice after 24 hr of stimulation with 100 ng/ml and 1 µg/ml LPS.
source: The results showed that the amounts of IL-6 secreted by microglial cells from homozygous IL-37 transgenic (IL-37tg/tg) mice were significantly reduced compared to microglial cells from control mice after 24 hr of stimulation with 100 ng/ml and 1 µg/ml LPS and additionally also 6 hr after stimulation with 1 µg/ml LPS (F(2,11)=7.941 p=0.007; p=0.007; p=0.054; F(2,11)=3.915 p=0.052; p=0.043; p=0.359; F(2,9)=12.74 p=0.002; p=0.004; p=0.009) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Microglial cells from homozygous IL-37 transgenic mice showed significantly reduced amounts of IL-6 after 6 hr of stimulation with 1 µg/ml LPS.
source: The results showed that the amounts of IL-6 secreted by microglial cells from homozygous IL-37 transgenic (IL-37tg/tg) mice were significantly reduced compared to microglial cells from control mice after 24 hr of stimulation with 100 ng/ml and 1 µg/ml LPS and additionally also 6 hr after stimulation with 1 µg/ml LPS (F(2,11)=7.941 p=0.007; p=0.007; p=0.054; F(2,11)=3.915 p=0.052; p=0.043; p=0.359; F(2,9)=12.74 p=0.002; p=0.004; p=0.009) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Microglial cells from heterozygous IL-37 transgenic mice (IL-37wt/tg) showed decreased IL-6 secretion after 6 hr of stimulation with 1 µg/ml LPS.
source: Microglial cells from heterozygous IL-37 transgenic mice (IL-37wt/tg) also showed decreased IL-6 secretion, but only after 6 hr of stimulation with 1 µg/ml LPS (F(2,9)=12.74 p=0.002; p=0.009) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The immunosuppressive effect of transgenic expression of IL-37 on primary microglia was demonstrated by differences between hetero- and homozygous IL-37 transgenic mice.
source: Thus, the immunosuppressive effect of transgenic expression of IL-37 on primary microglia was demonstrated only in this experiment by differences between hetero- and homozygous IL-37 transgenic mice.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Primary microglial cells from IL-37tg mice showed significantly reduced release of TNF-α compared with primary microglial cells from control mice.
source: Further analysis also confirmed the reduction in inflammatory mediators by measuring the release of IL-6 when other concentrations of the inflammatory stimulus were examined (Figure 1C) and could be extended by the significantly reduced release of TNF-α (Figure 1D) and IL-1β (Figure 1E), compared with primary microglial cells from control mice (IL-6: p=0.1007; p=0.0024; p=0.0001; TNF-α: p=0.0038; p<0.0001; p<0.0001; IL-1β: p=0.0295; p=0.0001; p<0.0001).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 1D.

claim: Primary microglial cells from IL-37tg mice showed significantly reduced release of IL-1β compared with primary microglial cells from control mice.
source: Further analysis also confirmed the reduction in inflammatory mediators by measuring the release of IL-6 when other concentrations of the inflammatory stimulus were examined (Figure 1C) and could be extended by the significantly reduced release of TNF-α (Figure 1D) and IL-1β (Figure 1E), compared with primary microglial cells from control mice (IL-6: p=0.1007; p=0.0024; p=0.0001; TNF-α: p=0.0038; p<0.0001; p<0.0001; IL-1β: p=0.0295; p=0.0001; p<0.0001).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 1E.

claim: LPS stimulation caused a detectable increase in the level of transgenic IL37 mRNA after 1 hr, which remained elevated up to 24 hr post stimulation.
source: Remarkably, LPS stimulation caused a detectable increase in the level of transgenic IL37 mRNA after 1 hr, which remained elevated in the following hours up to 24 hr post stimulation (F(7,15)=2.629 p=0.05509; p=0.0171, p=0.0086, p=0.0238) (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 1F.

claim: The amount of IL-6 protein in the supernatant of IL-37tg microglial cells was significantly reduced compared to identically stimulated control cells.
source: As mentioned previously, the amount of IL-6 protein in the supernatant of the same cultures was significantly reduced when IL-37tg microglial cells were compared to identically stimulated control cells (p<0.0001) (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 1G.

claim: Primary astrocytes from IL-37tg mice did not show decreased levels of IL-6 and TNF-α 24 hr after LPS stimulation (100 ng/ml) compared with WT primary astrocytic cells.
source: Examining inflammatory responses in primary astrocytes as a different group of glial cells, we did not detect decreased levels of IL-6 and TNF-α in IL-37tg cells 24 hr after LPS stimulation (100 ng/ml) compared with WT primary astrocytic cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B), confirming the importance of anti-inflammatory IL-37 signaling, which may proceed via microglia but not astrocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Primary WT microglial cells pretreated with 500 ng/mL rIL-37 showed a significant decrease in the release of IL-6 after LPS induction compared with cells pretreated with rIL-37 vehicle (PBS).
source: After LPS induction, microglial cells pretreated with the higher concentration of rIL-37 showed a significant decrease in the release of IL-6 compared with cells pretreated with rIL-37 vehicle (PBS) (F(2,30)=5.135 p=0.0121; p=0.0133; F(2,30)=3.512 p=0.0426; p=0.0498) (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 1H.

claim: Microglial cells release lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines upon acute inflammatory stimulation in the presence of IL-37.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that microglial cells in particular release lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines upon acute inflammatory stimulation in the presence of IL-37.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Succinate and itaconate are novel markers associated with pro-inflammatory macrophage activation and function.
source: Among them, the TCA cycle-related metabolites succinate and itaconate are novel markers associated with pro-inflammatory macrophage activation and function (He et al., 2021; Michelucci et al., 2021; Mills et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: Many metabolites were significantly elevated in LPS-treated control microglial cells, including itaconate and succinate.
source: As expected, many metabolites were significantly elevated in LPS-treated control cells, including itaconate and succinate, both metabolic markers for proinflammatory activation of macrophages (Figure 2A; Michelucci et al., 2021; Tannahill et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2A and supporting citations.

claim: Levels of itaconate and succinate were significantly less elevated in IL-37tg microglial cells after LPS treatment, indicating an attenuated pro-inflammatory response at the metabolic level.
source: Levels of both metabolites were significantly less elevated in IL-37tg microglial cells, indicating an attenuated pro-inflammatory response at the metabolic level (Figure 2B and C) (itaconate F(1,20)=174.9 p<0.0001; p<0.0001; p<0.0001; F(1,20)=27.55 p<0.0001; p<0.0001; succinate F(1,20)=98.40 p<0.0001; p<0.0001; p=0.0005; F(1,20)=17.01 p=0.0005; p<0.0001).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 2B and C.

claim: IL-37tg microglial cells release lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines than control cells after LPS stimulation.
source: We conclude that IL-37tg microglial cells release lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines than control cells after LPS stimulation and that IL-37 expression in microglial cells limits LPS-induced pro-inflammatory metabolic reprogramming.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: IL-37 expression in microglial cells limits LPS-induced pro-inflammatory metabolic reprogramming.
source: We conclude that IL-37tg microglial cells release lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines than control cells after LPS stimulation and that IL-37 expression in microglial cells limits LPS-induced pro-inflammatory metabolic reprogramming.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Both experimental groups showed significant weight loss in response to systemic LPS injection, but the effect was significantly higher in control mice than in IL-37tg mice.
source: Both experimental groups showed significant weight loss in response to systemic LPS injection, but the effect was significantly higher in control mice than in IL-37tg mice (weight loss F(1,17)=220.5 p<0.0001; p<0.0001; p<0.0001; F(1,41)=1.486 p=0.2299; p=0.0139) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Control mice treated with LPS had a significantly higher percentage of CD68-expressing microglial cells compared to the cells of control animals treated with saline.
source: Control mice treated with LPS had a significantly higher percentage of CD68-expressing microglial cells (gated on the CD11b+/CD45low population) (CD68 F(1,6)=19.52 p=0.0045; p=0.0017; p>0.9999; F(1,6)=48.42 p=0.0004; p=0.0001) (Figure 3C–D) compared to the cells of control animals treated with saline.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 3C–D.

claim: IL-1β levels in the brain of LPS-treated WT mice were significantly higher than those of saline-treated WT controls.
source: Similarly, IL-1β levels in the brain of LPS-treated WT mice were significantly higher than those of saline-treated WT controls (IL-1β F(1,7)=9.399 p=0.0182; p=0.0244; p=0.7541; F(1,7)=3.182 p=0.0935; p=0.0366) (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 3E.

claim: IL-37tg animals showed no significant changes in CD68-expressing microglia and IL-1β levels when challenged with LPS compared with matched controls.
source: Remarkably, IL-37tg animals showed no significant changes in CD68-expressing microglia and IL-1β levels when challenged with LPS in the same manner compared with matched controls (Figure 3C–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3C–E.

claim: A significant increase in the number of IBA-1 positive cells was observed in the CA1 subregion of the hippocampus and in the cortex of LPS-treated control animals compared with saline-treated control animals.
source: A significant increase in the number of IBA-1 positive cells was observed in the CA1 subregion of the hippocampus and in the cortex of LPS-treated animals compared with saline-treated control animals. However, in the IL-37tg mice, LPS did not result in a significant increase in the number of microglial cells (IBA-1 CA1 F(1,25)=5.222 p=0.0311; p=0.0024; p>0.9999; F(1,34)=4.951 p=0.0328; p=0.0027;; IBA-1 Cx F(1,25)=15.97 p=0.0005; p=0.0002; p=0.3234; F(1,34)=5.159 p=0.0296; p=0.0054) (Figure 3F and H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 3F and H.

claim: In IL-37tg mice, LPS did not result in a significant increase in the number of microglial cells in the CA1 subregion of the hippocampus and in the cortex.
source: A significant increase in the number of IBA-1 positive cells was observed in the CA1 subregion of the hippocampus and in the cortex of LPS-treated animals compared with saline-treated control animals. However, in the IL-37tg mice, LPS did not result in a significant increase in the number of microglial cells (IBA-1 CA1 F(1,25)=5.222 p=0.0311; p=0.0024; p>0.9999; F(1,34)=4.951 p=0.0328; p=0.0027;; IBA-1 Cx F(1,25)=15.97 p=0.0005; p=0.0002; p=0.3234; F(1,34)=5.159 p=0.0296; p=0.0054) (Figure 3F and H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 3F and H.

claim: The anti-inflammatory effect of IL-37 expression on brain after LPS challenge is possibly mediated via microglial cells.
source: Overall, these results demonstrate the anti-inflammatory effect of IL-37 expression on brain after LPS challenge, possibly mediated via microglial cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Acute hippocampal slices from control mice treated with LPS showed significantly impaired LTP compared to saline treated control mice.
source: After 20 minutes of baseline recording, we observed significantly impaired LTP in the acute hippocampal slices of control mice treated with LPS compared to saline (F(1,28)=4.459 p=0.0438) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 4A.

claim: IL-37tg animals treated with LPS did not show comparable deficits in synaptic plasticity compared to saline treated IL-37tg animals.
source: In contrast, IL-37tg animals treated with LPS did not show comparable deficits in synaptic plasticity compared to saline treated IL-37tg animals (F(1,23)=0.0849 p=0.7734) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 4B.

claim: A significant decrease in the density of dendritic spines of CA1 pyramidal neurons and dentate gyrus cells was observed in control mice treated with LPS compared with saline-treated mice.
source: A significant decrease in the density of dendritic spines of CA1 pyramidal neurons and dentate gyrus cells was observed in control mice treated with LPS compared with saline-treated mice (spines CA1 F(1,32)=22.81 p<0.0001; p<0.0001; p=0.1145; F(1,44)=26.68 p<0.0001; p<0.0001; spines DG F(1,26)=3.307 p=0.0805; p=0.0062; p>0.9999; F(1,36)=0.529 p=0.4718; p=0.0295) (Figure 4D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 4D–F.
